`lore-proto/README.md`:

```md
# Lore Protos

## Description

This crate contains the proto files and the build code to generate and expose a crate, using `prost` and `tonic`.
It also contains a package.json so the proto files can be published to artifactory.

## Publish
In order to publish do the following:

1. Go to the lore-proto folder:
```
cd lore-proto
```

2. Login to artifactory:
```
npm login --registry=<REGISTRY_URL> --auth-type=web
```
...and follow the instructions and login in the browser.

3. Version the package, changing the version number on `package.json` (e.g. 0.1.4). This should be in sync with the Cargo.toml version in this same folder.

4. Publish the package:
```
npm publish
```

5. Commit the updated package.json and Cargo.toml files to the repository.

```

`lore-proto/build.rs`:

```rs
// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Epic Games, Inc.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
use std::env;
use std::io::Result;
use std::path::Path;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;

/// Resolve the `protoc` binary the same way prost-build does: the `PROTOC`
/// environment variable if set, otherwise `protoc` from `PATH`.
fn protoc_path() -> PathBuf {
    env::var_os("PROTOC").map_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("protoc"), PathBuf::from)
}

/// Returns true if `protoc` can actually be executed. When it can't, the build
/// falls back to the pregenerated sources checked in under `src/grpc`.
fn protoc_available() -> bool {
    Command::new(protoc_path())
        .arg("--version")
        .output()
        .is_ok_and(|output| output.status.success())
}

/// Emit `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for every `.proto` under `dir` so the bindings
/// are regenerated only when an input actually changes.
fn rerun_if_proto_changed(dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
        let path = entry?.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            rerun_if_proto_changed(&path)?;
        } else if path.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("proto") {
            println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", path.display());
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let crate_dir = env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("No manifest dir set");
    let proto_dir = PathBuf::from(&crate_dir).join("proto");
    let output_dir = PathBuf::from(&crate_dir).join("src").join("grpc");

    // Declare the codegen inputs unconditionally so Cargo re-runs this script
    // when PROTOC changes or a watched .proto is edited — even on a build where
    // protoc is missing. Emitting these before the availability check is what
    // lets a fixed PROTOC (or a newly installed protoc plus a .proto edit)
    // recover and regenerate; if they were only emitted after the early return,
    // the protoc-missing run would record no watches and fixing PROTOC alone
    // would never re-run this script.
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=PROTOC");
    rerun_if_proto_changed(&proto_dir)?;

    // protoc is only needed to regenerate the gRPC bindings. When it isn't
    // installed, rely on the pregenerated sources committed under src/grpc so
    // the crate still builds.
    if !protoc_available() {
        return Ok(());
    }

    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    // Use Bytes for buffers instead of Vec
    config.bytes(["."]);

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &[
                "./proto/model.proto",
                "./proto/admin.proto",
                "./proto/lock.proto",
                "./proto/epic_events.proto",
                "./proto/lore_notification.proto",
                "./proto/notification.proto",
                "./proto/replication.proto",
            ],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    // lore.model.v1 — shared base types
    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    config.bytes(["."]);

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(config, &["./proto/lore/model/v1/model.proto"], &["./proto"])?;

    // lore.storage.v1 — storage service, references lore.model.v1 via extern_path
    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    config.bytes(["."]);
    config.extern_path(".lore.model.v1", "crate::lore::model::v1");

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &["./proto/lore/storage/v1/storage.proto"],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    // lore.revision.v1 — baseline revision-graph service, references lore.model.v1
    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    config.bytes(["."]);
    config.extern_path(".lore.model.v1", "crate::lore::model::v1");

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &["./proto/lore/revision/v1/revision.proto"],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    // lore.repository.v1 — repository-management service, references lore.model.v1
    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    config.bytes(["."]);
    config.extern_path(".lore.model.v1", "crate::lore::model::v1");

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &["./proto/lore/repository/v1/repository.proto"],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    // lore.thin_client.v1 — thin-client presentation helpers, references lore.model.v1.
    // model.proto and thin_client.proto share the same package and are compiled
    // together into a single generated module.
    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    config.bytes(["."]);
    config.extern_path(".lore.model.v1", "crate::lore::model::v1");

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &[
                "./proto/lore/thin_client/v1/model.proto",
                "./proto/lore/thin_client/v1/thin_client.proto",
            ],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    // lore.environment.v1 — server-side environment discovery service. Self-contained — declares its own messages
    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    config.enable_type_names();
    config.bytes(["."]);

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &["./proto/lore/environment/v1/environment.proto"],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    let mut config = tonic_prost_build::Config::new();
    // Use Bytes for buffers instead of Vec
    config.bytes(["."]);

    tonic_prost_build::configure()
        .out_dir(&output_dir)
        .protoc_arg("--experimental_allow_proto3_optional")
        .build_server(false)
        .compile_with_config(
            config,
            &["./proto/auth_api.proto", "./proto/rebac_api.proto"],
            &["./proto"],
        )?;

    Ok(())
}
```

`lore-proto/proto/lock.proto`:

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

import "google/protobuf/timestamp.proto";

package urc.lock;

// Represents the resource being locked in the repository
message Resource {
  // Branch ID
  bytes branch = 1;

  // Hash for the resource
  bytes hash = 2;

  // Human readable description of the resource (i.e. file path, property name,
  // etc)
  string description = 3;
}

// Represents the lock on a resource
message Lock {
  // Resource reference
  Resource resource = 1;

  // The server will store the user's ID provided with the
  // request's auth info
  string owner = 2;

  // Lock timestamp
  google.protobuf.Timestamp locked_at = 3;
}

service LockService {
  // Locks resources, errors if already locked
  rpc Lock(LockRequest) returns (LockResponse);

  // Query for locks
  rpc Query(QueryRequest) returns (QueryResponse);

  // Get lock status
  rpc Status(StatusRequest) returns (StatusResponse);

  // Unlocks resources, no-ops if no lock exists
  rpc Unlock(UnlockRequest) returns (UnlockResponse);

  // Locks resources for another user
  rpc AdminLock(AdminLockRequest) returns (AdminLockResponse);
}

  repeated Lock locks = 1;
}

  optional string owner = 2;
  optional string description = 3;

  repeated Lock locks = 1;
}

  repeated Resource resources = 1;
}
```

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package lore.environment.v1;

// Server-side environment discovery service. Clients call this once during
// connection setup to learn which auxiliary endpoints (storage, revision,
// lock, notification, ...) live at which URLs and to read server-tunable
// configuration (compression mode, query batch size). The service is
// unauthenticated — it does not depend on any per-repository state.
service EnvironmentService {
  // Fetch the server's current environment configuration. Servers in
  // maintenance mode respond with `Unavailable` and a message containing
  // "maintenance".
  rpc EnvironmentGet(EnvironmentGetRequest) returns (EnvironmentGetResponse);
}

// Per-service endpoint URLs. An empty string means "no override for this
// service"; clients fall back to the URL they were configured with. The
// server stores whatever the operator configured verbatim; URLs are
// expected to be fully-qualified (`scheme://host[:port][/path]`).
message Endpoint {
  // Authentication / authorisation token-exchange endpoint.
  string auth_url = 1;
  // Repository-management service endpoint.
  string repository_url = 2;
  // Storage service endpoint.
  string storage_url = 3;
  // Revision-graph service endpoint.
  string revision_url = 4;
  // Lock service endpoint.
  string lock_url = 5;
  // Notification service endpoint.
  string notification_url = 6;
}

// Compression algorithm to use when storing payloads.
enum CompressionMode {
  // Server has no opinion; the client picks based on its own configuration.
  NOT_SPECIFIED = 0;
  // Disable compression entirely.
  NO_COMPRESSION = 1;
  LZ4 = 2;
  OODLE = 3;
  ZSTD = 4;
}

// Server-tunable configuration knobs returned alongside the endpoint
// directory.
message Config {
  // Maximum number of addresses the server accepts in a single
  // `StorageService.Query` batch. `0` means "use the client default".
  uint32 max_query_batch = 1;
  // Preferred compression mode for new payloads. Unset means the server
  // has no opinion; the client's local configuration wins.
  optional CompressionMode compression_mode = 2;
}

// Composite environment record returned by EnvironmentGet.
message Environment {
  // Per-service endpoint URLs.
  Endpoint endpoint = 1;
  // Server-tunable configuration knobs.
  Config config = 2;
}

// Empty request envelope (the call has no parameters).
message EnvironmentGetRequest {}

// Response carrying the environment record.
message EnvironmentGetResponse {
  // The server's current environment configuration.
  Environment environment = 1;
}
```

`lore-proto/proto/lore/model/v1/model.proto`:

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package lore.model.v1;

// Storage fragment header — describes a unit of content-addressed payload
// returned from the storage layer.
message Fragment {
  // Implementation-defined fragment flags (compression, encryption, etc.).
  uint32 flags = 1;
  // Wire size of the fragment payload after any encoding (compressed bytes).
  uint32 size_payload = 2;
  // Logical size of the underlying content before encoding.
  uint64 size_content = 3;
}

// Content-addressed handle for a stored object.
message Address {
  // Content hash uniquely identifying the object.
  bytes hash = 1;
  // Optional addressing context (e.g. partition / namespace tag).
  bytes context = 2;
}

// Result of a fragment lookup against the storage layer.
enum FragmentState {
  // Found in the caller-supplied addressing context.
  FOUND_IN_CONTEXT = 0;
  // Found, but in a different context than the caller supplied.
  FOUND = 1;
  // No fragment exists at this address in any reachable context.
  NOT_FOUND = 2;
  // Lookup failed for an indeterminate reason.
  UNKNOWN = 3;
}

// Anchor identifying a specific revision on a specific branch by content
// signature. Used in Branch.stack (ancestry chain) and in any context where
// the revision must be concrete (e.g. BranchCreate's caller-supplied stack).
// Carries the signature only; callers needing the per-branch revision number
// look it up via RevisionInfo.
message BranchPoint {
  // Branch the parent revision lives on.
  bytes branch_id = 1;
  // Content signature of the parent revision.
  bytes revision_signature = 2;
}

// Request-time specifier for a revision. RevisionIdentifier is paired with
// `bytes signature` in oneof `query` / `query_<side>` / `start` fields per
// the unified revision-specifier convention.
message RevisionIdentifier {
  // Branch the revision lives on.
  bytes branch_id = 1;
  // Per-branch revision number. In any v1 *request*, value 0 resolves to
  // the current tip of the branch; the server resolves 0 to a concrete
  // number at request time. Valid Storage and response state always carry
  // concrete numbers; 0 never appears there.
  // Exception: BranchCreate requires fully-resolved concrete signatures via BranchPoint stack.
  // Exception: In responses, zeroed revision signatures resolve to a zeroed revision number
  uint64 number = 2;
}

// Lean projection of a revision used in list responses (e.g.
// RevisionListResponse.items). Carries enough to identify the revision
// and present a list-row entry without the full Revision payload.
message RevisionItem {
  // Revision number on its branch.
  uint64 number = 1;
  // Content signature of the revision.
  bytes signature = 2;
  // Metadata hash associated with this revision.
  bytes metadata = 3;
  // Serialized state header.
  bytes state = 4;
}

// A repository — the top-level container for a revision graph. Repositories
// are hard-deleted (no `deleted` flag): a deleted repository disappears
// from RepositoryGet / RepositoryList entirely and its name becomes free
// for reuse.
message Repository {
  // Server-assigned unique identifier; stable across renames.
  bytes id = 1;
  // Human-readable name. Unique among live repositories. Validation rules
  // are defined by lore-revision (see `repository::is_valid_name`).
  string name = 2;
  // Free-form caller-supplied description.
  string description = 3;
  // Default branch id, fixed at create time and stored in the repository
  // metadata blob.
  bytes default_branch_id = 4;
  // Default branch name, fixed at create time.
  string default_branch_name = 5;
  // Identity that created the repository (caller-supplied when permitted,
  // else the authenticated JWT identity).
  string creator = 6;
  // Server-assigned creation timestamp (Unix epoch seconds).
  uint64 created = 7;
  // Current metadata pointer hash; mutated atomically via
  // RepositoryMetadataSet.
  bytes metadata = 8;
}

// A branch in the revision graph. Tombstoned (deleted=true) branches are
// preserved by id but their name → id mapping is erased per the
// "Branch names are exclusive to live branches" invariant.
message Branch {
  // Server-assigned unique identifier; stable across renames and
  // deletion (tombstone preserves id).
  bytes id = 1;
  // Human-readable name. Unique among live branches; freed for reuse on
  // BranchDelete. Validation rules are defined by lore-revision.
  string name = 2;
  // Identity that created the branch (caller-supplied when permitted, else
  // the authenticated JWT identity).
  string creator = 3;
  // Free-form caller-defined tag for grouping or filtering branches by
  // intent. Server stores verbatim; no enforced vocabulary.
  string category = 4;
  // Server-assigned creation timestamp (Unix epoch seconds).
  uint64 created = 5;
  // Signature of the current branch tip.
  bytes latest = 6;
  // True iff the branch has been tombstoned via BranchDelete. The record
  // survives but the name → id lookup is erased.
  bool deleted = 7;
  // Current metadata hash; mutated atomically via BranchMetadataSet.
  bytes metadata = 8;
  // Ancestry chain — parent-first, root-last. stack[0] is the immediate
  // parent the branch was forked from; stack[N-1] is the ultimate root.
  repeated BranchPoint stack = 9;
}
```

`lore-proto/proto/lore/repository/v1/repository.proto`:

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package lore.repository.v1;

import "lore/model/v1/model.proto";

// Baseline repository-management service. Carries the lifecycle and
// metadata-pointer primitives — repository create / delete, lookup, list,
// and CAS update of the repository metadata pointer. The repository
// metadata blob itself is read/written through CAS storage like any other
// content; this service only mediates the pointer to its current head.
service RepositoryService {
  // Create a new repository together with its default branch. The caller
  // pre-generates `id` and `default_branch_id` for retry idempotency.
  // Re-issuing the same `id` (or `name`) returns ALREADY_EXISTS unless the
  // call is byte-for-byte the same as the prior one, in which case it
  // returns the existing record (idempotent retry).
  rpc RepositoryCreate     (RepositoryCreateRequest)     returns (RepositoryCreateResponse);
  // Hard-delete a repository: clears the name → id mapping, zeroes the
  // metadata pointer, and tears down all branches.
  rpc RepositoryDelete     (RepositoryDeleteRequest)     returns (RepositoryDeleteResponse);
  // Look up a repository by id or by name.
  rpc RepositoryGet        (RepositoryGetRequest)        returns (RepositoryGetResponse);
  // Stream all repositories the caller is authorised to see.
  rpc RepositoryList       (RepositoryListRequest)       returns (stream RepositoryListResponse);
  // Cheap hash-only read of a repository's current metadata pointer.
  rpc RepositoryMetadataGet(RepositoryMetadataGetRequest) returns (RepositoryMetadataGetResponse);
  // Compare-and-swap update of a repository's metadata pointer. CAS miss is
  // signalled in-band via the response, never as a non-OK gRPC status.
  rpc RepositoryMetadataSet(RepositoryMetadataSetRequest) returns (RepositoryMetadataSetResponse);
}

// Request to create a new repository. The caller pre-generates `id` and
// `default_branch_id` so retries are idempotent — a duplicate `id` yields
// ALREADY_EXISTS unless the call is byte-for-byte the same as the prior
// success, in which case the server returns the existing record.
message RepositoryCreateRequest {
  // Caller-pre-generated repository id (typically a UUIDv7).
  bytes id = 1;
  // Human-readable repository name. Must satisfy the validation rules in
  // `lore-revision::repository::is_valid_name` and must not collide with
  // any existing repository.
  string name = 2;
  // Free-form description, stored verbatim in the repository metadata.
  string description = 3;
  // Caller-pre-generated default branch id (typically a UUIDv7).
  bytes default_branch_id = 4;
  // Default branch name, e.g. "main". Subject to the same name-validation
  // limits as a regular branch name.
  string default_branch_name = 5;
  // Identity to attribute as the repository creator. If unset, the server
  // uses the authenticated JWT identity. If set, the caller must have
  // permission to attribute repositories to other identities.
  optional string creator = 6;
}

// Response containing the freshly-created repository record.
message RepositoryCreateResponse {
  // Full Repository record including server-assigned `created` timestamp
  // and the server-assigned metadata pointer.
  lore.model.v1.Repository repository = 1;
}

// Request to hard-delete a repository by id. Names are not used here
// because they may have been recycled after a prior delete.
message RepositoryDeleteRequest {
  // Repository id obtained from a prior RepositoryGet / RepositoryList.
  bytes id = 1;
}

// Response carrying the last-known repository record. Repositories are
// hard-deleted, so this is the caller's only chance to see the deleted
// record's id, name and creator.
message RepositoryDeleteResponse {
  // Repository record as it was immediately before deletion.
  lore.model.v1.Repository repository = 1;
}

// Request to look up a repository by id or by name.
message RepositoryGetRequest {
  // Lookup mode.
  oneof query {
    // Lookup by repository id.
    bytes id = 1;
    // Lookup by repository name.
    string name = 2;
  }
}

// Response containing the resolved repository record.
message RepositoryGetResponse {
  // Repository record matching the lookup.
  lore.model.v1.Repository repository = 1;
}

// Request to stream repositories the caller is authorised to see, with
// optional filters. When auth is configured the server first consults
// the auth service for the caller's permitted resource set; when auth is
// off the server returns all locally-known repositories.
message RepositoryListRequest {
  // If set, only repositories whose `creator` field is an exact
  // byte-for-byte case-sensitive match are emitted.
  optional string creator = 1;
}

// One-per-stream-message response carrying a single repository record.
message RepositoryListResponse {
  // A repository matching the request's filters and the caller's
  // authorisation.
  lore.model.v1.Repository repository = 1;
}

// Request for a cheap hash-only read of a repository's metadata pointer.
message RepositoryMetadataGetRequest {
  // Repository id.
  bytes id = 1;
}

// Response carrying the current metadata hash.
message RepositoryMetadataGetResponse {
  // Current metadata pointer.
  bytes metadata = 1;
}

// Request for a compare-and-swap update of a repository's metadata
// pointer. The proposed metadata blob must already be addressable in CAS
// before issuing this call; the server validates that any Address-typed
// values inside the blob reference live blobs and refuses to install a
// blob that mutates read-only fields (name, creator, created).
message RepositoryMetadataSetRequest {
  // Repository id.
  bytes id = 1;
  // The metadata hash the caller expects to be currently set. The server
  // compares this to the actual current value and only swaps on match.
  bytes expected = 2;
  // The metadata hash to install if the CAS succeeds.
  bytes updated = 3;
}

// Response always returned with gRPC OK regardless of CAS hit or miss. On
// a successful CAS, response.metadata == request.updated. On a CAS miss,
// response.metadata reflects the unchanged prior value; the caller compares
// response.metadata vs request.updated to detect the miss and retry.
message RepositoryMetadataSetResponse {
  // The repository's current metadata pointer after the call.
  bytes metadata = 1;
}
```

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package lore.revision.v1;

import "lore/model/v1/model.proto";

// Baseline revision-graph service. Carries the minimal, stable set of
// graph primitives — branch lifecycle, metadata CAS, revision listing.
// Presentation helpers (describe / tree / diff) live separately on
// lore.thin_client.v1.ThinClientService.
service RevisionService {
  // Create a new branch as a fork of an existing revision chain.
  rpc BranchCreate     (BranchCreateRequest)      returns (BranchCreateResponse);
  // Tombstone a live branch by id. Idempotent on already-tombstoned
  // branches.
  rpc BranchDelete     (BranchDeleteRequest)      returns (BranchDeleteResponse);
  // Look up a branch by id (live or tombstoned) or by name (live only).
  rpc BranchGet        (BranchGetRequest)         returns (BranchGetResponse);
  // Stream all branches matching the optional filters.
  rpc BranchList       (BranchListRequest)        returns (stream BranchListResponse);
  // Set the tip of a branch to a specific revision. Supports force and
  // fast-forward-merge semantics.
  rpc BranchPush       (BranchPushRequest)        returns (BranchPushResponse);
  // Cheap hash-only read of a branch's current metadata pointer.
  rpc BranchMetadataGet(BranchMetadataGetRequest) returns (BranchMetadataGetResponse);
  // Compare-and-swap update of a branch's metadata pointer. CAS miss is
  // signalled in-band via the response, never as a non-OK gRPC status.
  rpc BranchMetadataSet(BranchMetadataSetRequest) returns (BranchMetadataSetResponse);
  // Page through a branch's revision history. Server picks page size.
  rpc RevisionList     (RevisionListRequest)      returns (RevisionListResponse);
}

// Request to create a new branch. The caller must supply a fully-resolved
// ancestry stack (no `number == 0` tip resolution is performed for
// BranchCreate). The caller also pre-generates the branch `id` so that
// retries are idempotent — a duplicate `id` already in use returns
// ALREADY_EXISTS.
message BranchCreateRequest {
  // Caller-pre-generated branch id (typically a UUIDv7). Re-issuing the
  // same id on retry yields ALREADY_EXISTS rather than creating a
  // duplicate; this gives the RPC end-to-end retry idempotency.
  bytes id = 1;
  // Human-readable name for the new branch. Must not collide with any
  // live branch (tombstoned names are free for reuse).
  string name = 2;
  // Identity to attribute as the branch creator. If unset, the server
  // uses the authenticated JWT identity. If set, the caller must have
  // permission to attribute branches to other identities.
  optional string creator = 3;
  // Free-form caller-defined tag for grouping or filtering. Server
  // stores verbatim; empty string allowed.
  string category = 4;
  // Ancestry chain — parent-first, root-last. stack[0] is the
  // immediate parent the new branch is forked from. Every entry's
  // revision_signature must resolve to a known revision on its
  // branch_id.
  repeated lore.model.v1.BranchPoint stack = 5;
}

// Response containing the newly-created branch record.
message BranchCreateResponse {
  // Full Branch record including server-assigned `created` timestamp
  // and the preserved stack.
  lore.model.v1.Branch branch = 1;
}

// Request to tombstone a live branch by id. Names are not used here
// because they may have been recycled after a prior delete.
message BranchDeleteRequest {
  // Branch id obtained from a prior BranchGet / BranchList.
  bytes id = 1;
}

// Response carrying the post-delete branch record. The record's name
// field is preserved even though the name → id mapping has been
// erased.
message BranchDeleteResponse {
  // Tombstoned branch record (deleted = true).
  lore.model.v1.Branch branch = 1;
}

// Request to look up a branch by id or by name.
message BranchGetRequest {
  // Lookup mode.
  oneof query {
    // Lookup by branch id — returns the branch live or tombstoned.
    bytes id = 1;
    // Lookup by branch name — returns the live branch with that name
    // only. Tombstoned branches are not resolvable by name.
    string name = 2;
  }
}

// Response containing the resolved branch record.
message BranchGetResponse {
  // Branch record matching the lookup.
  lore.model.v1.Branch branch = 1;
}

// Request to stream branches with optional filters.
message BranchListRequest {
  // If set, only branches whose `creator` field is an exact
  // byte-for-byte case-sensitive match are emitted. If unset, no
  // creator filter is applied.
  optional string creator = 1;
  // If true, tombstoned branches are emitted with `Branch.deleted =
  // true`. Default false (only live branches emitted).
  bool include_deleted = 2;
}

// One-per-stream-message response carrying a single branch record.
message BranchListResponse {
  // A branch matching the request's filters.
  lore.model.v1.Branch branch = 1;
}

// Request to push a revision as a branch's new tip.
message BranchPushRequest {
  // Target branch id.
  bytes id = 1;
  // Content signature of the revision to push. Caller must ensure the
  // revision and all data it references are present in CAS before
  // calling.
  bytes revision_signature = 2;
  // When true, the server replaces the tip directly without checking
  // whether the new tip descends from the current one. Wins over
  // `fast_forward_merge` when both are set.
  bool force = 3;
  // When true and the new tip does not descend from the current tip,
  // the server attempts a fast-forward merge. Mutually superseded by
  // `force`.
  bool fast_forward_merge = 4;
}

// Response describing the resulting branch tip after a push.
message BranchPushResponse {
  // Signature of the resulting tip (may equal the request's
  // revision_signature, or a new merge revision in the
  // fast-forward-merge case).
  bytes revision_signature = 1;
  // Per-branch number of the resulting tip.
  uint64 revision_number = 2;
  // True iff the server performed a fast-forward merge to land the
  // push.
  bool fast_forward_merged = 3;
  // Optional human-readable diagnostic. Free-form; clients should not
  // parse it.
  optional string message = 4;
}

// Request for a cheap hash-only read of a branch's metadata pointer.
message BranchMetadataGetRequest {
  // Branch id.
  bytes id = 1;
}

// Response carrying the current metadata hash.
message BranchMetadataGetResponse {
  // Current metadata pointer.
  bytes metadata = 1;
}

// Request for a compare-and-swap update of a branch's metadata pointer.
message BranchMetadataSetRequest {
  // Branch id.
  bytes id = 1;
  // The metadata hash the caller expects to be currently set. The
  // server compares this to the actual current value and only swaps
  // on match.
  bytes expected = 2;
  // The metadata hash to install if the CAS succeeds.
  bytes updated = 3;
}

// Response always returned with gRPC OK regardless of CAS hit or miss.
// On a successful CAS, response.metadata == request.updated. On a CAS
// miss, response.metadata reflects the unchanged prior value; the
// caller compares response.metadata vs request.updated to detect the
// miss and retry.
message BranchMetadataSetResponse {
  // The branch's current metadata pointer after the call.
  bytes metadata = 1;
}

// Request to page through a branch's revision history. The start
// anchor selects which revision the page is anchored at; both forms
// resolve to the same concrete revision and walk that branch's
// history.
message RevisionListRequest {
  // Start anchor for the page.
  oneof start {
    // Identifier-based anchor; `number == 0` resolves to the tip of
    // the branch.
    lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier = 1;
    // Signature-based anchor (typically a cursor returned by a
    // previous response).
    bytes signature = 2;
  }
}

// Response carrying a page of revision items (newer-to-older within
// the page) plus optional cursors for the next pages in either
// direction.
message RevisionListResponse {
  // The page of revisions, newest-to-oldest. The revision identified by
  // the request's `start` anchor is guaranteed to appear somewhere in
  // the page, but is not necessarily items[0] — the server may align
  // the page on a wider boundary (e.g. a cached segment) and return
  // items both newer and older than the anchor. Server picks page size.
  repeated lore.model.v1.RevisionItem items = 1;
  // Cursor (signature) to feed back as `start.signature` to fetch
  // the page of revisions newer than this one. Unset when no further
  // newer revisions exist.
  optional bytes signature_forward = 2;
  // Cursor (signature) to feed back as `start.signature` to fetch
  // the page of revisions older than this one. Unset when no further
  // older revisions exist.
  optional bytes signature_backward = 3;
}
```

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package lore.thin_client.v1;

import "lore/model/v1/model.proto";

// File-system entry kind for tree listings and diff entries.
enum NodeType {
  // A directory.
  DIRECTORY = 0;
  // A regular file.
  FILE = 1;
  // A symbolic link.
  LINK = 2;
}

// Per-path action describing what happened between two states (or relative
// to the common ancestor in 3-way merges).
enum Action {
  // No change at this path.
  KEEP = 0;
  // The path was added.
  ADD = 1;
  // The path was removed.
  DELETE = 2;
  // The path was moved (rename + parent change).
  MOVE = 3;
  // The path was copied to a new location.
  COPY = 4;
}

// Type tag for a Metadata value, mirroring the corresponding urc enum.
enum MetadataType {
  // Address bytes (content reference).
  ADDRESS = 0;
  // Boolean value encoded as "true" / "false" string.
  BOOLEAN = 1;
  // Opaque binary value.
  BINARY = 2;
  // Addressing context bytes.
  CONTEXT = 3;
  // Hash bytes.
  HASH = 4;
  // Numeric value encoded as a string.
  NUMERIC = 5;
  // UTF-8 string value.
  STRING = 6;
}

// One per-path change in a revision diff. Replaces the old urc Path +
// PathDiff pair with a single "what happened to this path" entry.
// In 3-way mode wrapped inside DiffConflict, the change is rooted at the
// common ancestor.
message DiffChange {
  // Destination path (where the entry lives in the "to" side).
  string path = 1;
  // Source path for MOVE / COPY actions; empty otherwise.
  string path_from = 2;
  // What kind of change occurred at this path.
  Action action = 3;
  // The kind of node at `path` in the "to" side.
  NodeType node_type = 4;
  // Content address on the "from" side; empty if the action is ADD or
  // the side has no content here.
  bytes content_from = 5;
  // Content address on the "to" side; empty if the action is DELETE or
  // the side has no content here.
  bytes content_to = 6;
  // True when the server auto-resolved this change in 3-way mode (only
  // meaningful when the request set `autoresolve = true`).
  bool automerged = 7;
}

// Pair of per-path changes describing a 3-way merge conflict at a single
// path. Each side's change is rooted at the common ancestor: in particular
// `change_from.content_from == change_to.content_from` and both equal the
// resolved base's content address for that path.
message DiffConflict {
  // The change one side made relative to the common ancestor.
  DiffChange change_from = 1;
  // The change the other side made relative to the common ancestor.
  DiffChange change_to = 2;
}

// A single entry in a revision tree listing.
message TreeNode {
  // Repository-relative path of this entry.
  string path = 1;
  // Whether this entry is a directory, file, or link.
  NodeType node_type = 2;
  // Content address for FILE / LINK entries; unused for DIRECTORY.
  lore.model.v1.Address address = 3;
}

// Self-describing revision record. Carries the resolved RevisionIdentifier
// so callers querying by bare signature learn the resolved (branch, number)
// in the same response.
message Revision {
  // Content signature of this revision. Globally unique; never appears on
  // two branches.
  bytes signature = 1;
  // Resolved (branch, number) for this revision. Echoed by the server so
  // signature-only queries can recover the per-branch coordinates.
  lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier = 2;
  // Free-form commit message.
  string commit_message = 3;
  // Commit timestamp (Unix epoch seconds). Always commit time, never
  // authorship time.
  uint64 timestamp = 4;
  // Identity that originally created the revision.
  string created_by = 5;
  // Identity that committed the revision (may differ from created_by).
  string committed_by = 6;
  // Per-revision metadata entries.
  repeated Metadata metadata = 7;
  // Self-side parent (the predecessor on this revision's own branch).
  // Unset on a branch root; otherwise set.
  optional Parent parent_self = 8;
  // Other-side parent (only set on merge commits).
  optional Parent parent_other = 9;
  // Per-branch revision number.
  uint64 number = 10;

  // A parent reference grouping the parent revision's signature and
  // resolved identifier.
  message Parent {
    // Signature of the parent revision.
    bytes signature = 1;
    // Resolved (branch, number) for the parent revision.
    lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier = 2;
  }
}

// Typed metadata key/value pair associated with a Branch or Revision.
message Metadata {
  // Caller-defined key.
  string key = 1;
  // Encoded value; interpretation depends on `metadata_type`.
  string value = 2;
  // Type tag indicating how `value` should be parsed.
  MetadataType metadata_type = 3;
}

// File-content diff request. ContentDiff is server-streaming and operates
// purely on CAS addresses — no path field, no per-revision context.
message ContentDiffRequest {
  // Content address of the "from" side. Empty bytes represent
  // "no content" (e.g. file added).
  bytes address_from = 1;
  // Content address of the "to" side. Empty bytes represent
  // "no content" (e.g. file deleted).
  bytes address_to = 2;
  // Common ancestor's content address. Presence (set, non-empty)
  // triggers 3-way merge mode; absence gives 2-way unified diff. There
  // is no separate mode flag.
  optional bytes address_base = 3;
  // Number of context lines around each hunk in the unified diff
  // output. Server picks a default if unset.
  optional uint32 context_lines = 4;
  // When true, lines that differ only in trailing whitespace are
  // treated as equal for stat / change-detection purposes. The
  // displayed diff text uses original (un-normalised) content.
  bool ignore_whitespace_eol = 5;
  // When true, runs of internal whitespace are collapsed to a single
  // space before comparing for stat / change-detection purposes.
  bool ignore_whitespace_inline = 6;
  // Maximum size in bytes of the generated diff text. When exceeded,
  // the response header sets `truncated = true` and emits no chunks;
  // summary stats are still computed.
  optional uint64 max_diff_size = 7;
}

// Server-streamed response for ContentDiff. The first message MUST carry
// `payload.header`; subsequent messages carry `payload.chunk`. Server MUST
// NOT emit a ContentDiffResponse with `payload` unset.
message ContentDiffResponse {
  oneof payload {
    // Summary stats and mode flags, computed up-front and emitted first.
    ContentDiffHeader header = 1;
    // A chunk of diff text. Concatenating `chunk.diff` strings in
    // arrival order reproduces the full diff text.
    ContentDiffChunkResponse chunk = 2;
  }
}

// Header for a ContentDiff stream. Reports summary stats and short-circuit
// flags that may end the stream after the header.
message ContentDiffHeader {
  // Number of lines added (after any whitespace preprocessing).
  uint64 lines_added = 1;
  // Number of lines deleted (after any whitespace preprocessing).
  uint64 lines_deleted = 2;
  // True when the input is detected as binary; the stream emits no
  // chunks and stats are zero.
  bool binary = 3;
  // True when the generated diff would exceed `max_diff_size`; the
  // stream emits no chunks but stats are still reported.
  bool truncated = 4;
  // True only in 3-way mode when the merge produced conflict markers.
  bool has_conflicts = 5;
  // Number of conflict regions in the merged text (3-way only).
  uint32 conflict_count = 6;
}

// A single chunk of diff text. Server picks chunk boundaries on UTF-8
// character boundaries; clients MUST NOT assume line alignment. Reserved
// for future additive fields (hunk index, byte offsets, etc.) under
// proto3 append-only rules.
message ContentDiffChunkResponse {
  // Diff text for this chunk.
  string diff = 1;
}
```

`lore-proto/proto/lore/thin_client/v1/thin_client.proto`:

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package lore.thin_client.v1;

import "lore/model/v1/model.proto";
import "lore/thin_client/v1/model.proto";

// Thin-client presentation helpers — describe / tree / diff RPCs that are
// convenience helpers for clients that lack local cache or compute ( web UIs).
// Sits alongside the baseline lore.revision.v1.RevisionService and shares the
// same backing revision-graph state.
service ThinClientService {
  // Stream a unified diff or 3-way merge of two CAS blobs as header +
  // chunked text.
  rpc ContentDiff (ContentDiffRequest)  returns (stream ContentDiffResponse);
  // Return the full Revision record for a specific revision.
  rpc RevisionInfo(RevisionInfoRequest) returns (RevisionInfoResponse);
  // Stream a unified 2-way / 3-way diff between two revisions as
  // header + DiffChange / DiffConflict items.
  rpc RevisionDiff(RevisionDiffRequest) returns (stream RevisionDiffResponse);
  // Stream the file/directory tree at a revision as header + TreeNode
  // items.
  rpc RevisionTree(RevisionTreeRequest) returns (stream RevisionTreeResponse);
}

// Request to describe a single revision by identifier or signature.
message RevisionInfoRequest {
  oneof query {
    // Identifier-based lookup; `number == 0` resolves to the tip of
    // the branch.
    lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier = 1;
    // Signature-based lookup.
    bytes signature = 2;
  }
}

// Response carrying the resolved Revision record. Self-describing —
// includes the resolved RevisionIdentifier even when queried by
// signature.
message RevisionInfoResponse {
  // The full Revision record.
  Revision revision = 1;
}

// Request to diff two revisions. Server picks the diff mode (2-way vs
// 3-way) from revision metadata; callers do not declare it.
message RevisionDiffRequest {
  // "From" side specifier.
  oneof query_from {
    // Identifier-based "from" (`number == 0` = tip).
    lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier_from = 1;
    // Signature-based "from".
    bytes signature_from = 2;
  }
  // "To" side specifier.
  oneof query_to {
    // Identifier-based "to" (`number == 0` = tip).
    lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier_to = 3;
    // Signature-based "to".
    bytes signature_to = 4;
  }
  // When true and the server picks 3-way mode, auto-resolved
  // DiffChange entries are flagged via `automerged = true`. Silently
  // ignored in 2-way mode.
  bool autoresolve = 5;
}

// Header for a RevisionDiff stream. Echoes the resolved revisions so
// callers querying by signature learn the (branch, number) and vice
// versa. Optional `_base` fields are populated only when the server
// selected a 3-way diff.
message RevisionDiffHeader {
  // Resolved (branch, number) of the "from" side.
  lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier_from = 1;
  // Resolved signature of the "from" side.
  bytes signature_from = 2;
  // Resolved (branch, number) of the "to" side.
  lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier_to = 3;
  // Resolved signature of the "to" side.
  bytes signature_to = 4;
  // Resolved (branch, number) of the common ancestor base. Set only
  // in 3-way mode.
  optional lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier_base = 5;
  // Resolved signature of the common ancestor base. Set only in
  // 3-way mode.
  optional bytes signature_base = 6;
}

// Server-streamed response for RevisionDiff. First message carries
// `payload.header`; subsequent messages stream `DiffChange` always and
// `DiffConflict` only in 3-way mode.
message RevisionDiffResponse {
  oneof payload {
    // Header echoing the resolved revisions.
    RevisionDiffHeader header = 1;
    // A per-path change.
    DiffChange change = 2;
    // A 3-way merge conflict pair (3-way mode only).
    DiffConflict conflict = 3;
  }
}

// Request to walk the file/directory tree at a specific revision.
message RevisionTreeRequest {
  // Revision specifier.
  oneof query {
    // Identifier-based lookup; `number == 0` resolves to the tip of
    // the branch.
    lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier = 1;
    // Signature-based lookup.
    bytes signature = 2;
  }
  // If set and non-empty, only entries at or under this path are
  // emitted. The prefix itself is emitted as a DIRECTORY node when
  // it exists. If unset or empty, the walk covers the full tree from
  // the repository root.
  optional string path_prefix = 3;
  // If set, limits the depth of descent below the prefix root. 1
  // emits only direct children of the prefix root; 2 emits direct
  // children plus grandchildren; etc. 0 or unset means unbounded.
  optional uint32 max_depth = 4;
}

// Header for a RevisionTree stream. Echoes the resolved revision so
// callers querying by signature learn the (branch, number) and vice
// versa.
message RevisionTreeHeader {
  // Resolved (branch, number) of the revision being walked.
  lore.model.v1.RevisionIdentifier identifier = 1;
  // Resolved signature of the revision being walked.
  bytes signature = 2;
}

// Server-streamed response for RevisionTree. First message carries
// `payload.header`; subsequent messages stream `TreeNode` items in
// server-natural order.
message RevisionTreeResponse {
  oneof payload {
    // Header echoing the resolved revision.
    RevisionTreeHeader header = 1;
    // A tree entry (directory, file, or link).
    TreeNode node = 2;
  }
}
```

```proto
package urc.notification;

// An event published when a branch is created on the server

  repeated string tags = 1;

  // Reserved
  string reserved = 2;

  // Event payload
  oneof event {
    BranchPushed branch_pushed = 3;
    ResourceLocked resource_locked = 4;
    ResourceUnlocked resource_unlocked = 5;
    BranchDeleted branch_deleted = 6;
    BranchCreated branch_created = 7;
  }
}

message SubscribeRequest {
  string stream = 1;
}

message CreateStreamRequest {
  string name = 1;
}

message PublishRequest {
  Event event = 1;
  bool create_stream = 2;
}

message AckRequest {
  string acknowledgement_id = 1;
}

message SubscribeOrAckRequest {
  oneof message {
    SubscribeRequest subscribe = 1;
    AckRequest ack = 2;
  }
}

service NotificationService {
  rpc Subscribe (SubscribeRequest) returns (stream Event);
  rpc Publish (PublishRequest) returns (google.protobuf.Empty);
}

service NotificationAdminService {
  rpc CreateStream (CreateStreamRequest) returns (google.protobuf.Empty);
  rpc SubscribeWithAcks (stream SubscribeOrAckRequest) returns (stream Event);
}
```

```rs
// Branch type conversions

impl From<&BranchPoint> for crate::model::BranchPoint {
    fn from(point: &BranchPoint) -> Self {
        crate::model::BranchPoint {
            branch: point.branch.into(),
            revision: point.revision.into(),
        }
    }
}

impl From<crate::model::BranchPoint> for BranchPoint {
    fn from(point: crate::model::BranchPoint) -> Self {
        BranchPoint {
            branch: point.branch.into(),
            revision: point.revision.into(),
        }
    }
}

impl From<BranchMetadata> for crate::model::Branch {
    fn from(metadata: BranchMetadata) -> Self {
        let stack: Vec<crate::model::BranchPoint> = metadata
            .stack
            .iter()
            .map(crate::model::BranchPoint::from)
            .collect();
        let branch_point_deprecated = stack
            .first()
            .map(|parent| parent.revision.clone())
            .or(Some(Hash::default().into()));
        let parent_deprecated = stack
            .first()
            .map(|parent| parent.branch.clone())
            .or(Some(Context::default().into()));

        crate::model::Branch {
            id: metadata.id.into(),
            name: metadata.name,
            category: metadata.category,
            latest: metadata.latest.into(),
            creator: metadata.creator,
            created: metadata.created,
            branch_point_deprecated,
            parent_deprecated,
            stack,
        }
    }
}

impl From<crate::model::Branch> for BranchMetadata {
    fn from(metadata: crate::model::Branch) -> Self {
        let mut stack: Vec<BranchPoint> =
            metadata.stack.into_iter().map(BranchPoint::from).collect();
        if stack.is_empty()
            && let Some(parent) = metadata.parent_deprecated
            && let Some(branch_point) = metadata.branch_point_deprecated
        {
            stack.push(BranchPoint {
                branch: parent.into(),
                revision: branch_point.into(),
            });
        }
        BranchMetadata {
            id: metadata.id.into(),
            name: metadata.name.clone(),
            category: metadata.category.clone(),
            latest: metadata.latest.into(),
            creator: metadata.creator,
            created: metadata.created,
            stack,
        }
    }
}

                branch: lock.resource.branch.into(),
                hash: lock.resource.hash.into(),
                description: lock.resource.description,
            }),
            owner: lock.owner,
            locked_at: Some(prost_types::Timestamp {
                seconds: (lock.locked_at / 1000) as i64,
                nanos: ((lock.locked_at % 1_000) * 1_000_000) as i32,
            }),
        }
    }
}

impl From<&LockData> for crate::lock::Lock {
    fn from(lock: &LockData) -> Self {
        crate::lock::Lock {
            resource: Some(crate::lock::Resource {
                branch: lock.resource.branch.into(),
                hash: lock.resource.hash.into(),
                description: lock.resource.description.clone(),
            }),
            owner: lock.owner.clone(),
            locked_at: Some(prost_types::Timestamp {
                seconds: (lock.locked_at / 1000) as i64,
                nanos: ((lock.locked_at % 1_000) * 1_000_000) as i32,
            }),
        }
    }
}

impl From<crate::lock::Lock> for LockData {
    fn from(lock: crate::lock::Lock) -> Self {
        let resource = lock.resource.unwrap_or_default();
        LockData {
            resource: LockResource {
                branch: resource.branch.into(),
                hash: resource.hash.into(),
                description: resource.description,
            },
            owner: lock.owner,
            locked_at: lock
                .locked_at
                .map(|t| (t.seconds as u64 * 1000) + (t.nanos as u64 / 1_000_000))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
        }
    }
}

impl From<&crate::lock::Lock> for LockData {
    fn from(lock: &crate::lock::Lock) -> Self {
        let resource = lock
            .resource
            .as_ref()
            .map(|resource| LockResource {
                branch: resource.branch.as_ref().into(),
                hash: resource.hash.as_ref().into(),
                description: resource.description.clone(),
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        LockData {
            resource,
            owner: lock.owner.clone(),
            locked_at: lock
                .locked_at
                .map(|t| (t.seconds as u64 * 1000) + (t.nanos as u64 / 1_000_000))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
pub mod urc_auth_api_client {
    #![allow(
        unused_variables,
        dead_code,
        missing_docs,
        clippy::wildcard_imports,
        clippy::let_unit_value,
    )]
    use tonic::codegen::*;
    use tonic::codegen::http::Uri;
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct UrcAuthApiClient<T> {
        inner: tonic::client::Grpc<T>,
    }
    impl UrcAuthApiClient<tonic::transport::Channel> {
        /// Attempt to create a new client by connecting to a given endpoint.
        pub async fn connect<D>(dst: D) -> Result<Self, tonic::transport::Error>
        where
            D: TryInto<tonic::transport::Endpoint>,
            D::Error: Into<StdError>,
        {
            let conn = tonic::transport::Endpoint::new(dst)?.connect().await?;
            Ok(Self::new(conn))
        }
    }
    impl<T> UrcAuthApiClient<T>
    where
        T: tonic::client::GrpcService<tonic::body::Body>,
        T::Error: Into<StdError>,
        T::ResponseBody: Body<Data = Bytes> + std::marker::Send + 'static,
        <T::ResponseBody as Body>::Error: Into<StdError> + std::marker::Send,
    {
        pub fn new(inner: T) -> Self {
            let inner = tonic::client::Grpc::new(inner);
            Self { inner }
```

```rs
/// Result of a fragment lookup against the storage layer.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum FragmentState {
    /// Found in the caller-supplied addressing context.
    FoundInContext = 0,
    /// Found, but in a different context than the caller supplied.
    Found = 1,
    /// No fragment exists at this address in any reachable context.
    NotFound = 2,
    /// Lookup failed for an indeterminate reason.
    Unknown = 3,
}
impl FragmentState {
    /// String value of the enum field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    ///
    /// The values are not transformed in any way and thus are considered stable
    /// (if the ProtoBuf definition does not change) and safe for programmatic use.
    pub fn as_str_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::FoundInContext => "FOUND_IN_CONTEXT",
            Self::Found => "FOUND",
            Self::NotFound => "NOT_FOUND",
            Self::Unknown => "UNKNOWN",
        }
    }
    /// Creates an enum from field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    pub fn from_str_name(value: &str) -> ::core::option::Option<Self> {
        match value {
            "FOUND_IN_CONTEXT" => Some(Self::FoundInContext),
            "FOUND" => Some(Self::Found),
            "NOT_FOUND" => Some(Self::NotFound),
            "UNKNOWN" => Some(Self::Unknown),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
```

```rs
    /// Baseline repository-management service. Carries the lifecycle and
    /// metadata-pointer primitives — repository create / delete, lookup, list,
    /// and CAS update of the repository metadata pointer. The repository
    /// metadata blob itself is read/written through CAS storage like any other
    /// content; this service only mediates the pointer to its current head.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct RepositoryServiceClient<T> {
        inner: tonic::client::Grpc<T>,
    }
    impl RepositoryServiceClient<tonic::transport::Channel> {
        /// Attempt to create a new client by connecting to a given endpoint.
        pub async fn connect<D>(dst: D) -> Result<Self, tonic::transport::Error>
        where
            D: TryInto<tonic::transport::Endpoint>,
            D::Error: Into<StdError>,
        {
            let conn = tonic::transport::Endpoint::new(dst)?.connect().await?;
            Ok(Self::new(conn))
        }
    }
    impl<T> RepositoryServiceClient<T>
    where
        T: tonic::client::GrpcService<tonic::body::Body>,
        T::Error: Into<StdError>,
        T::ResponseBody: Body<Data = Bytes> + std::marker::Send + 'static,
        <T::ResponseBody as Body>::Error: Into<StdError> + std::marker::Send,
    {
        pub fn new(inner: T) -> Self {
            let inner = tonic::client::Grpc::new(inner);
            Self { inner }
        }
        pub fn with_origin(inner: T, origin: Uri) -> Self {
            let inner = tonic::client::Grpc::with_origin(inner, origin);
            Self { inner }
        }
        pub fn with_interceptor<F>(
            inner: T,
            interceptor: F,
        ) -> RepositoryServiceClient<InterceptedService<T, F>>
        where
            F: tonic::service::Interceptor,
            T::ResponseBody: Default,
            T: tonic::codegen::Service<
                http::Request<tonic::body::Body>,
                Response = http::Response<
                    <T as tonic::client::GrpcService<tonic::body::Body>>::ResponseBody,
                >,
            >,
            <T as tonic::codegen::Service<
                http::Request<tonic::body::Body>,
            >>::Error: Into<StdError> + std::marker::Send + std::marker::Sync,
        {
            RepositoryServiceClient::new(InterceptedService::new(inner, interceptor))
        }

        }
        /// Create a new repository together with its default branch. The caller

                    let max_encoding_message_size = self.max_encoding_message_size;

                                tonic::metadata::GRPC_CONTENT_TYPE,

                    })
                }
            }
        }
    }
```

```rs
// This file is @generated by prost-build.
/// One per-path change in a revision diff. Replaces the old urc Path +
/// PathDiff pair with a single "what happened to this path" entry.
/// In 3-way mode wrapped inside DiffConflict, the change is rooted at the
/// common ancestor.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct DiffChange {
    /// Destination path (where the entry lives in the "to" side).
    #[prost(string, tag = "1")]
    pub path: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    /// Source path for MOVE / COPY actions; empty otherwise.
    #[prost(string, tag = "2")]
    pub path_from: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    /// What kind of change occurred at this path.
    #[prost(enumeration = "Action", tag = "3")]
    pub action: i32,
    /// The kind of node at `path` in the "to" side.
    #[prost(enumeration = "NodeType", tag = "4")]
    pub node_type: i32,
    /// Content address on the "from" side; empty if the action is ADD or
    /// the side has no content here.
    #[prost(bytes = "bytes", tag = "5")]
    pub content_from: ::prost::bytes::Bytes,
    /// Content address on the "to" side; empty if the action is DELETE or
    /// the side has no content here.
    #[prost(bytes = "bytes", tag = "6")]
    pub content_to: ::prost::bytes::Bytes,
    /// True when the server auto-resolved this change in 3-way mode (only
    /// meaningful when the request set `autoresolve = true`).
    #[prost(bool, tag = "7")]
    pub automerged: bool,
}

/// Pair of per-path changes describing a 3-way merge conflict at a single

    /// The change the other side made relative to the common ancestor.

/// Self-describing revision record. Carries the resolved RevisionIdentifier
/// so callers querying by bare signature learn the resolved (branch, number)
/// in the same response.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct Revision {
    /// Content signature of this revision. Globally unique; never appears on
    /// two branches.
    #[prost(bytes = "bytes", tag = "1")]
    pub signature: ::prost::bytes::Bytes,
    /// Resolved (branch, number) for this revision. Echoed by the server so
    /// signature-only queries can recover the per-branch coordinates.
    #[prost(message, optional, tag = "2")]
    pub identifier: ::core::option::Option<crate::lore::model::v1::RevisionIdentifier>,
    /// Free-form commit message.
    #[prost(string, tag = "3")]
    pub commit_message: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    /// Commit timestamp (Unix epoch seconds). Always commit time, never
    /// authorship time.
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "4")]
    pub timestamp: u64,
    /// Identity that originally created the revision.
    #[prost(string, tag = "5")]
    pub created_by: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    /// Identity that committed the revision (may differ from created_by).
    #[prost(string, tag = "6")]
    pub committed_by: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    /// Per-revision metadata entries.
    #[prost(message, repeated, tag = "7")]
    pub metadata: ::prost::alloc::vec::Vec<Metadata>,
    /// Self-side parent (the predecessor on this revision's own branch).
    /// Unset on a branch root; otherwise set.
    #[prost(message, optional, tag = "8")]
    pub parent_self: ::core::option::Option<revision::Parent>,
    /// Other-side parent (only set on merge commits).
    #[prost(message, optional, tag = "9")]
    pub parent_other: ::core::option::Option<revision::Parent>,
    /// Per-branch revision number.
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "10")]
    pub number: u64,
}
/// Nested message and enum types in `Revision`.
pub mod revision {
    /// A parent reference grouping the parent revision's signature and
    /// resolved identifier.
    #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
    pub struct Parent {
        /// Signature of the parent revision.
        #[prost(bytes = "bytes", tag = "1")]
        pub signature: ::prost::bytes::Bytes,
        /// Resolved (branch, number) for the parent revision.
        #[prost(message, optional, tag = "2")]
        pub identifier: ::core::option::Option<
            crate::lore::model::v1::RevisionIdentifier,
        >,
    }
    impl ::prost::Name for Parent {
        const NAME: &'static str = "Parent";
        const PACKAGE: &'static str = "lore.thin_client.v1";
        fn full_name() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
            "lore.thin_client.v1.Revision.Parent".into()
        }
        fn type_url() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
            "/lore.thin_client.v1.Revision.Parent".into()
        }
    }
}
impl ::prost::Name for Revision {
    const NAME: &'static str = "Revision";
    const PACKAGE: &'static str = "lore.thin_client.v1";
    fn full_name() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "lore.thin_client.v1.Revision".into()
    }
    fn type_url() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "/lore.thin_client.v1.Revision".into()

/// File-content diff request. ContentDiff is server-streaming and operates
/// purely on CAS addresses — no path field, no per-revision context.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct ContentDiffRequest {
    /// Content address of the "from" side. Empty bytes represent
    /// "no content" (e.g. file added).
    #[prost(bytes = "bytes", tag = "1")]
    pub address_from: ::prost::bytes::Bytes,
    /// Content address of the "to" side. Empty bytes represent
    /// "no content" (e.g. file deleted).
    #[prost(bytes = "bytes", tag = "2")]
    pub address_to: ::prost::bytes::Bytes,
    /// Common ancestor's content address. Presence (set, non-empty)
    /// triggers 3-way merge mode; absence gives 2-way unified diff. There
    /// is no separate mode flag.
    #[prost(bytes = "bytes", optional, tag = "3")]
    pub address_base: ::core::option::Option<::prost::bytes::Bytes>,
    /// Number of context lines around each hunk in the unified diff
    /// output. Server picks a default if unset.
    #[prost(uint32, optional, tag = "4")]
    pub context_lines: ::core::option::Option<u32>,
    /// When true, lines that differ only in trailing whitespace are
    /// treated as equal for stat / change-detection purposes. The
    /// displayed diff text uses original (un-normalised) content.
    #[prost(bool, tag = "5")]
    pub ignore_whitespace_eol: bool,
    /// When true, runs of internal whitespace are collapsed to a single
    /// space before comparing for stat / change-detection purposes.
    #[prost(bool, tag = "6")]
    pub ignore_whitespace_inline: bool,
    /// Maximum size in bytes of the generated diff text. When exceeded,
    /// the response header sets `truncated = true` and emits no chunks;
    /// summary stats are still computed.
    #[prost(uint64, optional, tag = "7")]
    pub max_diff_size: ::core::option::Option<u64>,
}
impl ::prost::Name for ContentDiffRequest {
    const NAME: &'static str = "ContentDiffRequest";
    const PACKAGE: &'static str = "lore.thin_client.v1";
    fn full_name() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "lore.thin_client.v1.ContentDiffRequest".into()
    }
    fn type_url() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "/lore.thin_client.v1.ContentDiffRequest".into()
    }
}
/// Server-streamed response for ContentDiff. The first message MUST carry
/// `payload.header`; subsequent messages carry `payload.chunk`. Server MUST
/// NOT emit a ContentDiffResponse with `payload` unset.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct ContentDiffResponse {
    #[prost(oneof = "content_diff_response::Payload", tags = "1, 2")]
    pub payload: ::core::option::Option<content_diff_response::Payload>,
}
/// Nested message and enum types in `ContentDiffResponse`.
pub mod content_diff_response {
    #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Oneof)]
    pub enum Payload {
        /// Summary stats and mode flags, computed up-front and emitted first.
        #[prost(message, tag = "1")]
        Header(super::ContentDiffHeader),
        /// A chunk of diff text. Concatenating `chunk.diff` strings in
        /// arrival order reproduces the full diff text.
        #[prost(message, tag = "2")]
        Chunk(super::ContentDiffChunkResponse),
    }
}
impl ::prost::Name for ContentDiffResponse {
    const NAME: &'static str = "ContentDiffResponse";
    const PACKAGE: &'static str = "lore.thin_client.v1";
    fn full_name() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "lore.thin_client.v1.ContentDiffResponse".into()
    }
    fn type_url() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "/lore.thin_client.v1.ContentDiffResponse".into()
    }
}
/// Header for a ContentDiff stream. Reports summary stats and short-circuit
/// flags that may end the stream after the header.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct ContentDiffHeader {
    /// Number of lines added (after any whitespace preprocessing).
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "1")]
    pub lines_added: u64,
    /// Number of lines deleted (after any whitespace preprocessing).
    #[prost(uint64, tag = "2")]
    pub lines_deleted: u64,
    /// True when the input is detected as binary; the stream emits no
    /// chunks and stats are zero.
    #[prost(bool, tag = "3")]
    pub binary: bool,
    /// True when the generated diff would exceed `max_diff_size`; the
    /// stream emits no chunks but stats are still reported.
    #[prost(bool, tag = "4")]
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// True only in 3-way mode when the merge produced conflict markers.
    #[prost(bool, tag = "5")]
    pub has_conflicts: bool,
    /// Number of conflict regions in the merged text (3-way only).
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "6")]
    pub conflict_count: u32,
}

    const NAME: &'static str = "ContentDiffHeader";
    const PACKAGE: &'static str = "lore.thin_client.v1";

        "lore.thin_client.v1.ContentDiffHeader".into()
    }
    fn type_url() -> ::prost::alloc::string::String {
        "/lore.thin_client.v1.ContentDiffHeader".into()
    }
}

/// File-system entry kind for tree listings and diff entries.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum NodeType {
    /// A directory.
    Directory = 0,
    /// A regular file.
    File = 1,
    /// A symbolic link.
    Link = 2,
}
impl NodeType {
    /// String value of the enum field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    ///
    /// The values are not transformed in any way and thus are considered stable
    /// (if the ProtoBuf definition does not change) and safe for programmatic use.
    pub fn as_str_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Directory => "DIRECTORY",
            Self::File => "FILE",
            Self::Link => "LINK",
        }
    }
    /// Creates an enum from field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    pub fn from_str_name(value: &str) -> ::core::option::Option<Self> {
        match value {
            "DIRECTORY" => Some(Self::Directory),
            "FILE" => Some(Self::File),
            "LINK" => Some(Self::Link),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}
/// Per-path action describing what happened between two states (or relative
/// to the common ancestor in 3-way merges).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum Action {
    /// No change at this path.
    Keep = 0,
    /// The path was added.
    Add = 1,
    /// The path was removed.
    Delete = 2,
    /// The path was moved (rename + parent change).
    Move = 3,
    /// The path was copied to a new location.
    Copy = 4,
}
impl Action {
    /// String value of the enum field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    ///
    /// The values are not transformed in any way and thus are considered stable
    /// (if the ProtoBuf definition does not change) and safe for programmatic use.
    pub fn as_str_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Keep => "KEEP",
            Self::Add => "ADD",
            Self::Delete => "DELETE",
            Self::Move => "MOVE",
            Self::Copy => "COPY",
        }
    }
    /// Creates an enum from field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    pub fn from_str_name(value: &str) -> ::core::option::Option<Self> {
        match value {
            "KEEP" => Some(Self::Keep),
            "ADD" => Some(Self::Add),
            "DELETE" => Some(Self::Delete),
            "MOVE" => Some(Self::Move),
            "COPY" => Some(Self::Copy),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Request to walk the file/directory tree at a specific revision.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct RevisionTreeRequest {
    /// If set and non-empty, only entries at or under this path are
    /// emitted. The prefix itself is emitted as a DIRECTORY node when
    /// it exists. If unset or empty, the walk covers the full tree from
    /// the repository root.
    #[prost(string, optional, tag = "3")]
    pub path_prefix: ::core::option::Option<::prost::alloc::string::String>,
```

```rs
#[repr(i32)]
pub enum FragmentState {
    FoundInContext = 0,
    Found = 1,
    NotFound = 2,
    Unknown = 3,
}
impl FragmentState {
    /// String value of the enum field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    ///
    /// The values are not transformed in any way and thus are considered stable
    /// (if the ProtoBuf definition does not change) and safe for programmatic use.
    pub fn as_str_name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::FoundInContext => "FOUND_IN_CONTEXT",
            Self::Found => "FOUND",
            Self::NotFound => "NOT_FOUND",
            Self::Unknown => "UNKNOWN",
        }
    }
    /// Creates an enum from field names used in the ProtoBuf definition.
    pub fn from_str_name(value: &str) -> ::core::option::Option<Self> {
        match value {
            "FOUND_IN_CONTEXT" => Some(Self::FoundInContext),
            "FOUND" => Some(Self::Found),
            "NOT_FOUND" => Some(Self::NotFound),
            "UNKNOWN" => Some(Self::Unknown),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}
```

`lore-proto/tests/v1_lint.rs`:

```rs
// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Epic Games, Inc.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
//! Lint / negative checks for the v1 proto surface. Walks the source
//! `.proto` files and asserts the unified-naming + structural rules
//! that the v1 RFC pins.

use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

const V1_PROTO_FILES: &[&str] = &[
    "proto/lore/model/v1/model.proto",
    "proto/lore/repository/v1/repository.proto",
    "proto/lore/revision/v1/revision.proto",
    "proto/lore/thin_client/v1/model.proto",
    "proto/lore/thin_client/v1/thin_client.proto",
];

fn read_v1(rel: &str) -> String {
    let crate_dir = env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR");
    let path = PathBuf::from(crate_dir).join(rel);
    fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read {}: {e}", path.display()))
}

fn non_comment_lines(content: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
    content.lines().filter(|line| {
        let trimmed = line.trim();
        !trimmed.starts_with("//") && !trimmed.is_empty()
    })
}

#[test]
fn no_urc_references() {
    for file in V1_PROTO_FILES {
        let content = read_v1(file);
        for line in non_comment_lines(&content) {
            assert!(
                !line.contains("urc."),
                "{file}: line `{line}` references a `urc.` type; v1 must not depend on urc"
            );
            assert!(
                !line.starts_with("import \"model.proto\"")
                    && !line.starts_with("import \"revision.proto\""),
                "{file}: imports a top-level urc proto; v1 must only import `lore/...` paths"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_repository_id_field() {
    for file in V1_PROTO_FILES {
        let content = read_v1(file);
        for line in non_comment_lines(&content) {
            assert!(
                !line.contains("repository_id"),
                "{file}: line `{line}` mentions `repository_id`; v1 requests must keep scoping out-of-band"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_urc_deprecated_field_names() {
    let forbidden = [
        "revision_deprecated",
        "parent_deprecated",
        "branch_point_deprecated",
    ];
    for file in V1_PROTO_FILES {
        let content = read_v1(file);
        for line in non_comment_lines(&content) {
            for name in &forbidden {
                assert!(
                    !line.contains(name),
                    "{file}: line `{line}` uses deprecated urc field name `{name}`"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_adjective_first_side_qualifiers() {
    // Field-decl detection: `<type> <name> = <num>;`. For each field name,
    // assert it does not start with a side qualifier followed by `_`.
    let qualifiers = ["from", "to", "self", "other", "base"];
    for file in V1_PROTO_FILES {
        let content = read_v1(file);
        for line in non_comment_lines(&content) {
            let trimmed = line
                .trim()
                .trim_start_matches("optional ")
                .trim_start_matches("repeated ");
            let Some((decl, _)) = trimmed.split_once('=') else {
                continue;
            };
            // decl looks like "<type> <name> "
            let Some(name) = decl.split_whitespace().nth(1) else {
                continue;
            };
            for q in &qualifiers {
                let prefix = format!("{q}_");
                assert!(
                    !name.starts_with(&prefix),
                    "{file}: field `{name}` uses adjective-first side qualifier `{q}_*`; \
                     v1 expects noun-first form (e.g. `signature_{q}` not `{q}_signature`)"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_dropped_rpcs_or_messages() {
    let dropped = [
        "BranchProtect",
        "BranchUnprotect",
        "BranchRevisionList",
        "RevisionStateHistory",
    ];
    for file in V1_PROTO_FILES {
        let content = read_v1(file);
        for d in &dropped {
            for marker in [format!("rpc {d}"), format!("message {d}")] {
                assert!(
                    !content.contains(&marker),
                    "{file}: contains `{marker}`; this RPC/message was dropped from v1"
                );
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn doc_comments_on_messages_and_enums() {
    for file in V1_PROTO_FILES {
        let content = read_v1(file);
        let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().collect();
        for (i, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            let trimmed = line.trim();
            let introduces_top_level = (trimmed.starts_with("message ")
                || trimmed.starts_with("enum ")
                || trimmed.starts_with("service "))
                && trimmed.ends_with('{');
            // Skip nested types — keep the check on top-level / one-level-nested
            // declarations (covers Revision.Parent at one nest level too).
            if !introduces_top_level {
                continue;
            }
            // Find the previous non-blank line; it must start with `//`.
            let mut found_doc = false;
            for j in (0..i).rev() {
                let prev = lines[j].trim();
                if prev.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                found_doc = prev.starts_with("//");
                break;
            }
            assert!(
                found_doc,
                "{file}: declaration on line {} is missing a `//` doc comment: `{trimmed}`",
                i + 1
            );
        }
    }
}
```
